full_text_en:
Qingdao Aucma Group Sales Company v. Lijin Branch of Bank of China — dispute over bill payment

Promulgated by the Supreme People's Court on June 20, 2000 (Fa Gong [2000] No. 26)

Supreme People's Court of the People's Republic of China
Civil Judgment

(2000) Jing Zhong Zi No. 72

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): Qingdao Aucma Group Sales Company. Domicile: Aucma Industrial Park, Economic and Technological Development Zone, Qingdao, Shandong Province.
Legal representative: Yin Yanzeng, General Manager of the company.
Agent ad litem: Bian Yimin, lawyer of Beijing Minzheng Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance): Lijin Branch of Bank of China. Domicile: Jin'er Road, Lijin County, Shandong Province.
Person in charge: Zhang Jufen, Branch Manager.
Agent ad litem: Guo Feng, lawyer of Beijing Dingming Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Ding Wenshun, lawyer of Shandong Minshun Law Firm.

The appellant, Qingdao Aucma Group Sales Company (hereinafter referred to as Aucma Sales Company), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (1999) Lu Fa Jing Chu Zi No. 42 rendered by the Shandong High People's Court in the case of dispute over bill payment with the respondent, Lijin Branch of Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as Lijin Bank of China). This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and conducted the trial, which has now been concluded.

Facts Found by the Court:

On March 13, 1998, Aucma Sales Company and Lijin County Materials Supporting Company (hereinafter referred to as Lijin Materials Company) entered into an industrial and mineral products purchase and sale contract, stipulating that Aucma Sales Company would supply Aucma series products to Lijin Materials Company with a total supply value of RMB 100,000,000, and the settlement method was bank acceptance bills. For this purpose, on March 14, 1998, Lijin Materials Company and Lijin Bank of China signed 20 bank acceptance agreements numbered 98001-1 to 98001-20, each providing: the acceptance bill amount was RMB 5,000,000; the applicant for acceptance (Lijin Materials Company) should pay the full amount of the bill to the accepting bank (Lijin Bank of China) seven days before the maturity date; if the applicant fails to pay the full amount before the maturity date, the accepting bank shall convert the shortfall into overdue loans. Lijin Materials Company and Lijin Bank of China affixed their seals to each of the above 20 acceptance agreements. On the same day, Lijin Materials Company, Lijin Bank of China, Aucma Sales Company, and Qingdao Aucma Electric Appliance Company (hereinafter referred to as Aucma Electric Appliance Company) signed a bank acceptance guarantee agreement, stipulating: Aucma Sales Company and Aucma Electric Appliance Company shall bear joint and several liability for the bank acceptance agreements numbered 98001-1 to 98001-20 signed between Lijin Bank of China and Lijin Materials Company; if Lijin Materials Company defaults, Lijin Bank of China has the right to directly claim against the guarantors, and Aucma Sales Company and Aucma Electric Appliance Company guarantee to settle the debt within five business days after receiving written notice from Lijin Bank of China; if the guarantors fail to repay the matured debt on time, Lijin Bank of China has the right to instruct the guarantors' depository financial institutions to directly deduct deposits from their accounts or directly seize other property rights of the guarantors, and may charge a penalty of 2% of the total guarantee amount based on the circumstances. Lijin Materials Company, Lijin Bank of China, Aucma Sales Company, and Aucma Electric Appliance Company each affixed their seals to the contract. On March 28, 1998, the Lijin County Notary Office of Shandong Province notarized the above bank acceptance guarantee agreement.

After the agreements were signed, Lijin Bank of China issued 20 bank acceptance bills to Lijin Materials Company as agreed, numbered VI100103276 to VII00103295. Each bill indicated: drawer: Lijin Materials Company, payee: Aucma Sales Company, drawee: Lijin Bank of China, amount: RMB 5,000,000, date of issue: March 14, 1998, maturity date: September 14, 1998, and each bill bore the notation "non-negotiable". Lijin Bank of China affixed its seal in the acceptor column of the above bills. On September 5 and September 10 of the same year, because Aucma Sales Company had not fully supplied the goods, it returned 11 of the bills totaling RMB 55,000,000 to Lijin Bank of China in two batches. Subsequently, on September 10 and 11, Aucma Sales Company presented the remaining 9 bank acceptance bills numbered VII00103276 to VI100103284, totaling RMB 45,000,000, for payment through its three depository banks to Lijin Bank of China. Lijin Bank of China refused payment on the grounds of "an agreed creditor-debtor relationship with Aucma Sales Company and Aucma Sales Company's default", meanwhile detained the bills, and issued a refusal certificate on September 23. On September 28, 1998, Aucma Sales Company issued a "Return Bill Explanation" to Lijin Bank of China and the Credit Management Department of Bank of China Shandong Branch, stating: "Due to objective market conditions, our company failed to fulfill the guarantee liability under the 'Bank Acceptance Guarantee Agreement' for the RMB 45,000,000 bank acceptance bills accepted by your bank. However, the purchase and sale business between our company and Lijin Materials Company is continuing. In view of the above, we hereby return the matured RMB 45,000,000 bank acceptance bills. We hope that after reporting to the superior for approval, corresponding bank acceptance bills can be issued anew." Lijin Bank of China then stamped "VOID" on the above bills and treated them as voided.

On July 5, 1999, Aucma Sales Company filed a lawsuit with the Shandong High People's Court, requesting a judgment ordering Lijin Bank of China to bear the payment liability for the above RMB 45,000,000 bank acceptance bills and to compensate for the corresponding losses.

The Shandong High People's Court held in its trial: The literal and abstract nature of negotiable instruments determines that once a bill is accepted, the acceptor is obligated to pay unconditionally at maturity, and no other reasons can be used as a ground for refusal. Aucma Sales Company, as the holder, presented the matured bills accepted by Lijin Bank of China for payment, and Lijin Bank of China refused payment and detained the bills on the ground that Aucma Sales Company had not fulfilled its guarantee obligation under the acceptance guarantee agreement, which was erroneous. Aucma Sales Company could have continued to claim the right of payment against Lijin Bank of China, or could have requested Lijin Bank of China to return the bills, but instead, on September 28, 1998, Aucma Sales Company issued a written "Return Bill Explanation" to Lijin Bank of China. The exercise of rights on a negotiable instrument is premised on holding the instrument; without the instrument, there is no right on the instrument. Aucma Sales Company's "Return Bill Explanation" returned the bills, which recorded its rights, to Lijin Bank of China, indicating that Aucma Sales Company abandoned the right to request the return of the bills, as well as the right of payment against Lijin Bank of China. This was an expression of Aucma Sales Company's waiver of the bills and the rights thereon, and a release of Lijin Bank of China's payment obligation. Such an act of waiving one's own rights and releasing the debtor's obligation does not violate legal provisions and should be valid. Therefore, from the time Lijin Bank of China received the "Return Bill Explanation", Aucma Sales Company had lost all rights to the above bills, and the creditor-debtor relationship between it and Lijin Bank of China arising from the above bills was terminated. After the termination of the negotiable instrument relationship with Lijin Bank of China, Aucma Sales Company filed a lawsuit again, requesting Lijin Bank of China to bear payment liability based on the instrument relationship, which should not be supported. After deliberation by the judicial committee of the court, the court rendered a judgment: Dismissing Aucma Sales Company's claims. The court acceptance fee for the first instance was RMB 265,010, to be borne by Aucma Sales Company.

Aucma Sales Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Shandong High People's Court, appealed to this Court, arguing: The "Return Bill Explanation" issued by Aucma Sales Company was directed at the RMB 55,000,000 bills returned on September 10, 1998, not the accepted RMB 45,000,000 bills. In this regard, testimony from the former legal representative and typist of Aucma Sales Company can prove that the "RMB 45,000,000" in the "Return Bill Explanation" was a clerical error and should be "RMB 55,000,000". With respect to the instrument relationship, returning bills and whether to accept the return are matters of rights and obligations between the drawer and the holder. The bill is a certificate of payment method between the parties, and testimony from Lijin Materials Company on January 28, 2000 can prove that for the RMB 45,000,000 bills, the company did not authorize anyone to retrieve them on its behalf. The reason Lijin Bank of China refused payment was that Aucma Sales Company had a creditor-debtor relationship with it. However, this creditor-debtor relationship was based on the "Bank Acceptance Guarantee Agreement" signed among Aucma Sales Company, Lijin Materials Company, and Lijin Bank of China. According to the "Bank Acceptance Agreement" between the parties and Article 91 of the People's Bank of China's "Measures for Settlement of Payment", Lijin Materials Company should have paid the full amount of the bills into Lijin Bank of China's account before the maturity date. Otherwise, Lijin Bank of China would convert the unpaid portion into overdue loans. That is, Aucma Sales Company assumed joint and several liability for the bills converted into overdue loans, not as a guarantor for the RMB 45,000,000 bank acceptance bills. Only when the loan is disbursed and the borrower fails to repay on time can the guarantor assume guarantee liability. Since the funds involved in this case were not loaned out, Aucma Sales Company had no guarantee liability. Instrument guarantee and loan guarantee are two different legal relationships. Lijin Bank of China's refusal to pay on the ground that the applicant for acceptance, Lijin Materials Company, had not repaid and Aucma Sales Company had assumed guarantee liability lacked legal basis. The first instance judgment found unclear facts and applied law incorrectly, requesting the cancellation of the original judgment and a judgment ordering Lijin Bank of China to bear payment liability for the RMB 45,000,000 bills involved in this case.

Lijin Bank of China responded: The first instance judgment found clear facts and correctly applied the law, requesting that it be affirmed.

Opinion of the Court:

The nine bank acceptance bills involved in this case are complete in form, with all necessary particulars fully recorded, conforming to Article 22 of the Negotiable Instruments Law of the People's Republic of China and relevant provisions, and should be deemed valid. To accept the bills in question, Lijin Materials Company and Lijin Bank of China, and Lijin Materials Company, Lijin Bank of China, Aucma Sales Company, and Aucma Electric Appliance Company respectively signed the "Acceptance Agreement" and "Acceptance Guarantee Agreement". Lijin Bank of China accepted the nine bills in accordance with the acceptance agreement, while also noting "non-negotiable", essentially providing financing for Lijin Materials Company's purchase of goods from Aucma Sales Company. Aucma Sales Company and Aucma Electric Appliance Company provided guarantees to Lijin Bank of China for this financing by Lijin Materials Company and undertook that Lijin Bank of China had the right to directly deduct the guarantors' property, thus placing themselves in the position of joint debtors bearing the same debt as the drawer. It was precisely on the basis of this underlying relationship existing between Lijin Bank of China and Aucma Sales Company that Lijin Bank of China invoked the defense to refuse payment. According to Article 13, paragraph 2 of the Negotiable Instruments Law of the People's Republic of China: "A debtor on a negotiable instrument may set up a defense against the holder who fails to perform the agreed obligations and who has a direct creditor-debtor relationship with such debtor." Under the circumstances provided by the above legal provision, a party to a negotiable instrument may use the underlying relationship of the instrument to counter the instrument relationship. Therefore, where the drawer, Lijin Materials Company, did not transfer the relevant funds into the account of the drawee, Lijin Bank of China, before the maturity date as agreed, and the holder, Aucma Sales Company, still presented the bills to the drawee (acceptor) for payment, the drawee, Lijin Bank of China, could exercise the right of defense on the basis of the relationship of funds to refuse to bear the corresponding payment liability. Pursuant to Article 99 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "if the parties mutually owe matured debts and the subject matter of such debts is of the same kind and quality, either party may set off its own debt against the debt of the other party", Lijin Bank of China's exercise of the right of set-off has a legal basis. The "Return Bill Explanation" issued by Aucma Sales Company also indicates the consensus reached between the parties to set off their respective debts. Aucma Sales Company's filing of a lawsuit after terminating the negotiable instrument relationship with Lijin Bank of China is manifestly improper. Its appeal argument that "instrument guarantee and loan guarantee are two different legal relationships, and since the loan involved in this case was not disbursed, Aucma Sales Company had no guarantee liability" lacks legal basis and is not supported by this Court. In summary, the first instance judgment found clear facts and properly dismissed Aucma Sales Company's claim that Lijin Bank of China should bear payment liability for the bills involved in this case. Pursuant to Article 13 and Article 22 of the Negotiable Instruments Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 99 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 153, paragraph 1(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court renders the following judgment:

Judgment:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The court acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 265,010, to be borne by Aucma Sales Company.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Li Tianshun
Trial Judge: Xu Ruibai
Acting Trial Judge: Wang Tao

May 31, 2000

Clerk: Li Guohui
